response:
Reflection and diagnosis: the archive now shows a sharp trade-off. Conditioner refinements that improve *ordering* (dp on non-current assets fmb 3.57, chronic count fmb 3.62, downside-only fmb 3.20, impairment-adjusted book fmb 3.27) all deliver near-zero or negative alpha, while the original magnitude conditioner ZSCORE(WINSOR(dp/at − MA3)) keeps alpha at 4.1–4.9% with Sharpe ~0.51. The reading is that the cross-sectional slope is generated by *who* deviates while the abnormal return is generated by *how much* they deviate — the extreme-magnitude tail contains the firms with genuinely large recognition shifts. The other lever that raised alpha was adding an independent liquidity condition (bounded composite: alpha 6.3%, t=5.34), but it halved Sharpe and left the slope flat, so the liquidity channel is a tail/factor-loading effect. Consolidation for the remaining generations should therefore hold the magnitude conditioner fixed and attack the two remaining sources of improvement: a cleaner value leg (industry-neutral cheapness, never tested) and explicit combination of the magnitude channel with the ordering channel, plus one benchmark alternative (distance from peak recognition) and one cumulative-stock formulation that repairs the failed book-side embedding by reusing it as a conditioner rather than as the value anchor.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Industry Neutral Cheapness With Discretion
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness is only informative relative to firms with comparable asset lives and capital intensity, so ranking EBITDA yield within industry isolates genuine mispricing rather than the permanent multiple differences between capital-intensive and asset-light sectors, and the depreciation-discretion conditioner then operates on a homogeneous set of candidates.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every version of the winning family has used an unconditional cross-sectional value rank, which loads the long leg on structurally low-multiple industries whose returns FF5's HML already spans, so industry-neutralizing the value leg is the one untested design choice that can raise abnormal return and Sharpe simultaneously rather than trading one metric for the other. It also aligns the two legs, since the conditioner's economic meaning — depreciation policy relative to a norm — is inherently within-industry.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Magnitude Plus Chronicity Discretion
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm is most credibly mispriced when its depreciation charge is both currently far above its norm and has been above it repeatedly, because a single large deviation can be an asset-mix accident while a persistent pattern reveals a conservative reporting policy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive has cleanly separated the two statistical roles — magnitude carries the alpha (4.9%, t=4.76, Sharpe 0.51) and chronicity carries the cross-sectional slope (fmb 3.62) — and these are different functions of the same underlying deviation, so summing their standardized versions is a targeted attempt to obtain both forms of evidence rather than a generic composite. Because both legs derive from one economic channel they should reinforce rather than dilute, unlike the earlier composites that mixed accounting policy with balance-sheet liquidity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Discretion Magnitude With Bounded Liquidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), ZSCORE(RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Honest capital-consumption accounting and a cash buffer covering near-term obligations are complementary requirements for a cheap firm to be a bargain, but the liquidity condition is informative only ordinally — being in the safe part of the distribution — whereas the accounting condition is informative in magnitude.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-5 bounded composite ranked *both* channels and produced the archive's largest alpha (6.3%, t=5.34) but collapsed Sharpe to 0.16, whereas the magnitude-only depreciation signal preserved Sharpe at 0.51; this variant keeps depreciation in magnitude form and bounds only the liquidity channel, isolating which side of the earlier composite destroyed risk-adjusted return. It is the informative middle case between the two archived designs rather than another arbitrary recombination.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Slide From Peak Recognition
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), TS_MAX(RATIO(dp, at), 5)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Under-recognition accumulates gradually, so the informative benchmark is the highest depreciation intensity the firm has ever sustained: a cheap firm still charging near its historical peak has nothing deferred, while one whose charge has drifted far below its own peak has been progressively capitalizing costs that a moving average partially absorbs into the benchmark.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: A three-year moving average is contaminated by the very drift it is meant to detect — a firm that cuts depreciation each year pulls its own benchmark down and looks innocent — whereas a five-year maximum is a ratchet benchmark immune to that contamination. This is a different benchmark concept rather than a rescaling, and because the measure retains magnitude it should preserve the tail behaviour that generates alpha in this family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Hidden Depreciation Shortfall Per Price
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(MUL(at, MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically relevant quantity is the accumulated dollar amount of depreciation a firm has failed to charge, measured against what investors are paying: a cheap firm carrying a large hidden shortfall relative to its market value faces an earnings reset that the low multiple has not discounted, while one with no accumulated shortfall is cheap on clean numbers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Capitalizing the shortfall over three years and scaling by market capitalization converts the annual policy deviation into a stock of overstatement expressed in the same units as the valuation, which is the natural way to compare the size of the accounting problem to the size of the discount. It repairs the gen-5 failure in which the same cumulative quantity was subtracted from book equity and produced a strong slope but no alpha, by using it as a conditioner on cheapness rather than as the value anchor itself.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Conjunctive Discretion And Liquidity Screen
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm escapes the value-trap classification only if it passes both tests — honest depreciation and cash cover of near-term obligations — so its score should be set by whichever condition it satisfies least, since a large cash pile cannot compensate for inflated earnings and vice versa.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-5 composite tested these two conditions additively, which lets a strong score on one channel mask failure on the other; the MIN operator implements the genuinely conjunctive version of the same economic claim and therefore tests whether the trap classification is about weakest-link failure or about an average of virtues. This is the correct place to revisit MIN, since the earlier weakest-link failure applied it to value and safety *levels*, whereas here the value leg remains multiplicative and only the two signed quality conditions are combined conjunctively.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Industry Neutral Cheapness With Discretion---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A single-operator change (RANK→IND_RANK) to the archive's best-performing template, but industry-neutralizing the value leg is economically motivated, untested here, and directly targets the HML/industry-tilt explanation for the family's alpha, so it is a legitimate if incremental test.

---CRITIQUE Magnitude Plus Chronicity Discretion---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent and sign-coherent, but the two legs are near-redundant functions of the identical deviation (level versus its own sign count), so the composite will likely track the magnitude version closely and the claim that FMB slope and FF5 alpha will simply add across correlated legs is unsupported.

---CRITIQUE Discretion Magnitude With Bounded Liquidity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is an ablation of the archived gen-5 SUMRANK composite that differs only in whether one of the two legs is rank-bounded, and ZSCORE(RANK(x)) is a monotone rescaling of RANK(x), making it a cosmetic interpolation between two already-evaluated designs rather than a new economic hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Slide From Peak Recognition---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Replacing the self-contaminating moving-average benchmark with a ratchet TS_MAX is a genuinely different measurement concept with a clear rationale, though it overlaps conceptually with the archived downside-only discretion signal (which had a strong slope but negligible alpha) since the deviation is one-sided by construction.

---CRITIQUE Hidden Depreciation Shortfall Per Price---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Expression matches the hypothesis and the NEG gives the correct positive expected sign, but scaling the shortfall by market cap when the value leg is already an inverse-market-cap yield builds a mechanical double 1/price (size) tilt into the product that could drive any result and should be diagnosed if the signal performs.

---CRITIQUE Conjunctive Discretion And Liquidity Screen---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: MIN of two un-recentered z-scores has a strongly negative mean, so for the large majority of firms the conditioner is negative and the product loads *negatively* on cheapness, inverting the intended interaction for most of the cross-section — the same construction defect that plausibly produced the archived Weakest Link Value Solvency signal's negative alpha.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Long Lived Asset Utilization Within Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, SUB(at, act)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm whose long-lived assets still turn over a normal volume of revenue owns productive capacity that the market is discounting, whereas a cheap firm generating little revenue per dollar of fixed assets is carrying idle or obsolete capacity whose book value will eventually be written down — the operating counterpart of the accounting-recognition trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the liquidity ablation entirely and opens an asset-utilization channel the archive has never tested, measuring whether the depreciable base is economically employed rather than how it is depreciated or how much cash sits beside it. Levels rather than growth rates keep it clear of the asset-growth confound, and industry z-scoring is required because revenue per fixed asset is an order of magnitude different across sectors, so the conditioner captures within-industry underutilization.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Recentered Conjunctive Quality Screen
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm qualifies as a bargain only if it clears both hurdles — depreciation charged at least in line with its own norm and cash covering near-term obligations — so its quality score should be the weaker of the two conditions, with firms failing either one classified as traps.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The critic's objection was purely a construction defect: MIN of two un-recentered z-scores has a strongly negative mean, so the product loaded negatively on cheapness for most firms, exactly the flaw behind the archived weakest-link inversion. Wrapping the MIN in an outer ZSCORE restores a zero mean so that roughly half the cross-section receives positive weight on cheapness and half negative, which preserves the intended long leg of cheap-and-doubly-clean firms and short leg of cheap-and-failing firms while keeping the conjunctive economics that distinguishes this test from the archived additive composite.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
